periods.analysis: Community Policing Expansion is green at 18% complete, establishing the operating base for a careful, trust-first rollout. The District 3 substation is open, and the foot-patrol pilot is complete in the Harbor Point and Cedar-Bay corridors, giving officers a regular presence without making the program feel like a surge operation. Community liaison officer hiring remains in progress with a 30-day milestone window, while the program evaluation report to council is appropriately not started with 120 days still ahead. The early read is steady: residents are seeing the same officers on the same blocks, and that consistency is the point.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green trajectory by locking the Harbor Point and Cedar-Bay foot-patrol routes into the next 90-day deployment plan rather than treating them as temporary coverage. Complete the liaison-officer interview panels with neighborhood association observers present, and document selection criteria before final offers are made. Begin setting up the evaluation file now by capturing baseline call-for-service, complaint, and community-meeting attendance data, even though the council report has not started.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 18% to 24%, a 6-point quarter-over-quarter increase, and the initiative remains green. The District 3 substation is now functioning as more than a storefront; roll-call briefings, youth-services referrals, and walk-in intake are being logged there on a consistent schedule. The completed foot-patrol pilot gave us usable lessons on shift timing, especially the value of 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. coverage around the ferry lots and the Cedar-Bay retail strip. Liaison hiring is still in progress within the 30-day window, and the council evaluation report remains not started with 120 days to go, which is acceptable at this stage if the evidence trail is maintained.
periods.recommendations: Keep the same two-corridor patrol pattern through the holiday retail period, but add a documented supervisor check at the midpoint of each foot shift. Move the liaison hiring file from screening to conditional selection, with background packets prioritized through HR batch CP-24-11. Have the substation sergeant send a monthly one-page trust log to the Public Safety analyst so the future council report is not built from memory.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 24% to 30%, another 6-point gain, and remains green. Winter operations tested whether the District 3 substation could hold community access when evening foot traffic dropped, and the answer was yes: officers shifted some contacts indoors through scheduled tenant-council and school-family nights. The foot-patrol pilot remains complete, but its practices are being translated into standard operating guidance for the two original corridors before any wider deployment. Liaison officer hiring remains in progress with the 30-day milestone still the active watch point, and the evaluation report to council is still not started with 120 days ahead.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the pace by issuing a short patrol-contact protocol for Harbor Point and Cedar-Bay before expanding to a third corridor. Close the remaining liaison-officer hiring steps by assigning one HR recruiter and one police-background investigator to the file until the 30-day item is resolved. Continue collecting resident-contact themes by shift and location, with particular attention to whether indoor meetings are reaching residents who do not attend precinct-wide forums.

periods.analysis: Community Policing Expansion moved from 30% to 36%, maintaining the established 6-point quarter-over-quarter progress and staying green. Spring and early summer activity increased contacts around beach access, Little League fields, and the marina bus loop, and the District 3 team handled that volume without abandoning the measured engagement model. The completed foot-patrol pilot is now informing beat cards for Officers Nguyen, Patel, and Rios, who have been assigned recurring blocks rather than rotating randomly. Hiring for community liaison officers remains in progress within the 30-day milestone, and the evaluation report remains not started with 120 days still available.
periods.recommendations: Extend the proven foot-patrol model to weekend afternoon coverage at the marina bus loop, but only after supervisors confirm it does not dilute the two pilot corridors. Keep community liaison hiring on the chief’s weekly agenda until offer letters and start dates are settled. Prepare the council-report framework now—metrics, resident feedback categories, and equity checks—while leaving the formal report in not-started status until the proper milestone window.

periods.analysis: The initiative increased from 36% to 42%, again a 6-point gain, and remains green. One year in, the District 3 substation is functioning as a stable neighborhood platform rather than a launch announcement, with front-counter referrals, patrol briefings, and community room reservations all tracked in the same log. Summer conditions brought more visitor-related calls near the waterfront, but the foot-patrol practices from Harbor Point and Cedar-Bay helped officers separate nuisance issues from genuine safety concerns. Liaison officer hiring is still in progress with the 30-day item open, and the program evaluation report to council remains not started with 120 days to go.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by formalizing the two pilot corridors as Training Route CP-D3-A and CP-D3-B for new community-policing assignments. Use September community meetings to test whether residents can name their assigned officers; that recognition measure should be included in the eventual council evaluation. Escalate liaison hiring bottlenecks through HR’s public-safety vacancy review so the open 30-day milestone does not become a trust issue.

periods.analysis: Progress moved from 42% to 48%, continuing the 6-point quarter-over-quarter pattern, with status still green. The program is now in the disciplined middle phase: the visible pieces are established, but the work is about repeatability, documentation, and not overpromising. The District 3 substation supported holiday-season retail walks along Cedar-Bay and coordinated with code compliance on after-hours business contacts, which kept the engagement posture consistent. Community liaison officer hiring remains in progress within the 30-day milestone, and the evaluation report to council remains not started with 120 days remaining.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the holiday foot-patrol schedule through the first two weeks of January, then compare complaint, arrest, and voluntary-contact data against the same corridors from the prior quarter. Assign a deputy chief to clear any remaining liaison-officer hiring approvals and report weekly until the 30-day milestone is closed. Build a draft data appendix for the council evaluation now, including substation walk-ins, meeting attendance, and resolved referral counts.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced from 48% to 54%, a 6-point gain, and remains green. The pace is appropriate for Harborview’s growth: fast enough to expand trust-building capacity, but controlled enough to preserve procedural fairness and officer familiarity. District 3 substation operations are now mature enough that the department can distinguish routine community contacts from problem-location interventions, which will matter when the evaluation report begins. The foot-patrol pilot remains complete, liaison hiring remains in progress with the 30-day item open, and the program evaluation report to council remains not started with 120 days ahead.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by adding a quarterly supervisor audit of body-worn-camera tagging for community-policing contacts, focused on consistency rather than discipline. Prepare the next expansion decision using a ranked list of candidate corridors, including South Marina, Northgate Village, and Bayview High, with call volume and resident-feedback criteria shown side by side. Keep pressure on liaison hiring, and pair any new liaison with an experienced District 3 officer for the first 60 days of community introductions.

periods.analysis: Community Policing Expansion moved from 54% to 60%, maintaining the steady 6-point quarter-over-quarter improvement and remaining green. At 60% complete, the initiative has shifted from proof of concept to managed expansion, with the District 3 substation, completed two-corridor foot-patrol pilot, and repeatable contact practices carrying the work. The department has preserved the central obligation: residents should experience this as access and accountability, not saturation. Community liaison officer hiring remains in progress with the 30-day milestone still active, and the program evaluation report to council remains not started with 120 days available.
periods.recommendations: Continue the green trajectory by authorizing one additional corridor only after the Harbor Point and Cedar-Bay measures show stable resident contact, complaint, and response-time patterns for two consecutive months. Set a firm internal deadline for the liaison-officer hiring milestone and publish the assignment plan to neighborhood leaders once selections are final. Start the evaluation work plan with named owners, data sources, and council-review dates so the 120-day report milestone begins cleanly when activated.

periods.analysis: 90% complete. 3 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: Program evaluation report to council (due Nov 23, 2026).
periods.recommendations: No action needed. Continue on the current plan.
